explicitDifferences: PLAIN embedded NUL rejected locally; upstream Response concatenates
Locale validated against broker offer locally; upstream sends configured value
Local candidate, initial-response, frame and JSON limits
AMQPLAIN table order normalized for semantic comparison only
Overlapping credential updates are rejected by the local concurrency policy
No-op unbind of never-bound auto-delete exchange: Node retains recovery record, pinned Go forgets it; real broker retains entity in both runs
Single-channel recovery follows cross-channel recorded dependencies here; pinned Go omits sibling-owned queues or routes in two verified scenarios
Pinned Go Confirm(true) sends no-wait bit but still waits; Node completes locally and receives subsequent real publisher confirmation. Go Confirm(false) used in the other eight broker comparisons.
Pinned Go only rejects negative integers and truncates count/size to uint16/uint32. Node rejects values outside the wire ranges before sending.
Pinned Go notifies the application but still allows Publish while paused. The MoonBit Session enforces server channel.flow(false) for new publications; Node exposes the notification as well.

At a withheld qos-ok boundary Go sends context-triggered basic.cancel concurrently; Node queues automatic cancellation until the current RPC reply. The Go probe ends at the observed wire boundary, without asserting success or failure of concurrent Go RPC replies.
Go keeps the old context watcher after manual cancellation; cancelling it stops a new consumer reusing the same tag. Node releases the watcher with its subscription.

With the reconnect proxy blocked, Go cancellation returns on the closed channel and leaves consumer recovery intent, so the consumer is restored. Node removes cancelled consumer intent while retaining queue/exchange topology without broker acknowledgement. Cancellation after completed recovery matches Go.

Node preserves its existing tag-zero/multiple all-outstanding interpretation. The fixed Go reference leaves handles pending until the later explicit cumulative tag; the 60 ms probe and subsequent completion are recorded separately.

Node preserves fail-closed validation of a future broker confirmation tag. The fixed Go reference keeps the connection open and waits for a valid tag; the invalid-tag probe does not establish a broker-supported workflow.

outboundStreaming.api: Session.publish_start/publish_body and Node Channel.publishStream; declared UInt64 body length, sync/async Uint8Array sources
outboundStreaming.frameBound: At most 64 KiB body per bridge call, also limited by negotiated frame_max minus 8
outboundStreaming.ordering: Per-channel content and later commands serialized; shared connection writer waits for socket drain; at most one source chunk read ahead
outboundStreaming.limits: Per-channel copied buffered bodies, socket writableLength and deferred protocol bytes each capped by maxBufferedBytes; queued operation and unconfirmed limits also enforced
outboundStreaming.failure: Partial source mismatch/error/timeout/cancel closes connection; broker channel close preserves siblings; queued abort does not iterate source; interrupted streams are not replayed
outboundStreaming.close: Graceful connection close drains prior channel writes and waits for pending publisher confirms; explicit channel close should follow awaiting publication
outboundStreaming.memoryScope: Source-owned storage, bridge temporaries, OS/TLS buffers and garbage collection excluded; no process RSS bound
outboundStreaming.brokerLimit: Pinned RabbitMQ default max message size 16 MiB: 32 MiB refused with 406, verified healthy sibling stays usable
outboundStreaming.receiveBoundary: Default incoming/return assembly remains 8 MiB; streamBodies opt-in now supports bounded streaming get/consume/return
outboundStreaming.cliBoundary: CLI stdin publication still buffers up to 1 MiB; legacy MoonBit content_frames/Session.publish helpers retain 1 MiB cap

inboundStreaming.api: Optional stream_bodies Session mode and Node streamBodies connection flag; MessageStart/Data/End and single-pass async Buffer iterable
inboundStreaming.completion: Header delivered early; completed verifies exact UInt64 body length; early ack/nack/reject refused; discard/break drains without broker acknowledgement
inboundStreaming.backpressure: Shared byte and 4096-chunk high watermarks; one 64 KiB decode batch per event-loop turn; maximum retained body bytes HWM + negotiated frameMax + 65536; chunk bound 12289; at most 1024 retained bodies and 64 incomplete content channels
inboundStreaming.socketInput: One pending input chunk up to 1 MiB; decoder and bridge storage bounded separately by frame/input limits
inboundStreaming.failure: Incomplete bodies fail on protocol error, timeout, channel/connection closure; completed buffered streams survive unexpected connection closure; callback errors and unobserved returns discard unread bodies
inboundStreaming.heartbeat: Receive deadline suspended only for application backpressure, outgoing heartbeats and body-progress timeout continue; per-batch yield preserves unrelated connections
inboundStreaming.recovery: Streaming consumer callbacks may run during recovery to drain TCP; recoveryReady awaited after body before acknowledgements; old stream and old tag never attached to new delivery
inboundStreaming.memoryScope: Bounds describe library-retained body bytes/chunks, not caller storage, encoding temporaries, kernel/TLS buffers or process RSS
inboundStreaming.legacy: Default Buffer reception keeps 8 MiB cap; file/raw CLI now streams. Frame-inspection CLI and legacy body helper retain 1 MiB cap.

commands: publish QUEUE (stdin spooled to private file)
cliStreaming.resources: Default 1 GiB configurable positive UInt64 body/disk quota; 64 KiB file and output-helper chunks, streaming client bounds still apply; not a process RSS bound
cliStreaming.output: Synced same-directory temporary file installed with exclusive hard link before ack; unsupported hard links or existing/raced targets fail without replacing them; raw stdout written by one cancellable Node helper process with one outstanding chunk
cliStreaming.failure: Controlled errors remove temporary files; interrupted or failed receive is not acknowledged; complete saved files or raw prefixes may remain if later steps fail; no exactly-once transaction or automatic retry
cliStreaming.platform: Actual Windows Node 24.11 with local WSL RabbitMQ; handled signal exits supported but native Windows force-kill cleanup is not guaranteed
cliStreaming.limits: No power-loss/filesystem-fault durability or forced-kill cleanup guarantee; arbitrary stalled filesystem calls may not be cancellable; source files must not be concurrently changed

verificationReuse.scope: All listed prior native/broker reports rerun on current engine/client/recovery sources; stored authentication vectors hash-checked and executed by core tests. Other 19 projects not retested.

noWait.completion: Ordered local socket send after pre-send backpressure wait; no RPC reply slot/timer, not a socket-drained or broker-acceptance guarantee; later channel errors asynchronous
noWait.returns: Queue name is requested name; message/consumer counts are unobserved zero placeholders; anonymous queue name stays empty
noWait.consumers: Register before send, rollback local failures, cap 1024; late/unknown deliveries dropped and streamed body drained without ack; cancel alone does not requeue prior unacked deliveries
noWait.recovery: Record sent intent, retain declaration/binding/consumer noWait flags; deletions update local intent; confirm mode restore waits normally; async broker failure can disagree with local topology intent

differences.name: confirm-no-wait
differences.explanation: Pinned Go confirmSelect.wait() returns true despite the wire Nowait bit. RabbitMQ suppresses the reply; Go did not return within a 300 ms observation and was closed explicitly. Node completes locally and receives a real publisher confirmation.

noWait.brokerComparisonScope: 15 independent-peer wire frames and 8 real broker scenarios match. Go uses Confirm(false) in those broker scenarios to isolate its separately reported Confirm(true) waiting difference; Node uses no-wait confirms. Named recovery, delayed errors, anonymous queue and cancellation/requeue covered. No complete API or throughput parity claim.

apiSurfaceAudit.scope: Syntactic exported-name functions/methods on exported receiver types in root non-test Go files. Includes conditional Fuzz; excludes unexported receivers and does not inventory struct fields, constants, interfaces or generated behavior. No full compatibility or coverage percentage claim.

channelOptions.qos: Backward-compatible qos(count,global,{prefetchSize}); UInt16/UInt32 ranges validated before send, snapshots restored per global setting before consumer replay
channelOptions.consume: noLocal bit independent of noWait/noAck/exclusive; retained during recovery; no client-side filtering of same-connection publications
channelOptions.publish: immediate flag independent of mandatory in buffer and stream APIs; additive MoonBit optional arguments and JS bridge exports preserve older signatures
channelOptions.flow: flow(active) controls broker delivery direction and returns actual reply bool; not replayed on recovery. Server flow event forwarded by both channel types, core replies automatically and refuses new publication while paused; already-started body completes before reply
channelOptions.broker: RabbitMQ 4.0.5 returns connection-level 540 for nonzero prefetchSize, immediate and flow(false); immediate message absence checked separately. flow(true) succeeds; noLocal accepts same-connection messages including after recovery

differences.name: qos-out-of-wire-range
differences.explanation: Pinned Go only rejects negative integers and truncates count/size to uint16/uint32. Node rejects values outside the wire ranges before sending.

differences.name: automatic-publisher-pause
differences.explanation: Pinned Go notifies the application but still allows Publish while paused. The MoonBit Session enforces server channel.flow(false) for new publications; Node exposes the notification as well.

channelOptions.comparisonScope: 18 exact method frames, one flow notification/reply sequence and nine real broker results including unsupported options and recovery. Two explicit local range/pause differences, not matches. RabbitMQ does not enforce noLocal isolation, rejects nonzero size/immediate/flow(false). No multiversion or throughput parity.

consumerCancellation.entry: consume(queue, callback, {signal}); raw and logical recovering subscriptions; pre-aborted signals rejected without sending
consumerCancellation.registration: Registration Promise settles after consume-ok/local noWait send; pending cancellation follows registration rather than revoking the consume RPC
consumerCancellation.completion: Waiting basic.cancel even for noWait subscription; callback null and cancel event with signal origin/reason; existing RPC and body sends drain first, one user RPC may wait behind automatic cancellation
consumerCancellation.ownership: Signal listener removed on manual/server cancellation, failures or closure; reused tags belong to a fresh subscription; signal preserved across completed recovery
consumerCancellation.offline: Remove consumer recovery intent immediately and notify with offline=true; retain queue/exchange topology without broker acknowledgement, no claim of complete offline auto-delete semantics
consumerCancellation.delivery: No automatic ack/requeue; already delivered incoming stream must still be read/discarded; cancelled deliveries after acknowledgement dropped without ack

differences.name: busy-rpc-scheduling
differences.explanation: At a withheld qos-ok boundary Go sends context-triggered basic.cancel concurrently; Node queues automatic cancellation until the current RPC reply. The Go probe ends at the observed wire boundary, without asserting success or failure of concurrent Go RPC replies.

differences.name: manual-reuse
differences.explanation: Go keeps the old context watcher after manual cancellation; cancelling it stops a new consumer reusing the same tag. Node releases the watcher with its subscription.

differences.name: offline-cancel
differences.explanation: With the reconnect proxy blocked, Go cancellation returns on the closed channel and leaves consumer recovery intent, so the consumer is restored. Node removes cancelled consumer intent while retaining queue/exchange topology without broker acknowledgement. Cancellation after completed recovery matches Go.

consumerCancellation.comparisonScope: Two independent-peer cancellation RPC sequences and nine real broker scenarios match. Three explicit differences cover a bounded RPC scheduling probe, tag reuse and offline cancellation; these are not matches. Offline cancellation retains queue/exchange topology without broker acknowledgement. No full context/API or throughput parity claim.

publicationSignalValidation: Reject non-AbortSignal values before consuming publication capacity; pre-fix repeated-invalid-input exhaustion reproduced and fixed in the existing local-failure fixture group

publisherConfirmations.entry: publishWithDeferredConfirm and publishStreamWithDeferredConfirm return a read-only handle after local send; null outside confirm mode. Existing publish methods retain waiting/rejection behavior
publisherConfirmations.handle: BigInt deliveryTag, completed/acked/error, non-rejecting done Promise and wait({signal,timeout}); nack/closure resolve false with error retained only for closure; independent waits do not retract messages
publisherConfirmations.limits: At most 1024 simultaneous waiters per handle; completed/cancelled waits release listeners. Unsequenced notification records share admission capacity with queued/unconfirmed publications
publisherConfirmations.notifications: Ordered confirm events plus split ack/nack events; individual handles may complete out of order; observer failures isolated and reported as callbackError; close discards buffered notices without synthetic broker nacks
publisherConfirmations.recovery: Physical generation 0; logical generations start at 1 and increase on channel replacement. Sequence resets to 1, listeners persist, old handles never bind to new publications
publisherConfirmations.sequence: nextPublishSeqNo is a snapshot, not a reservation; assignment occurs when send starts; logical offline query rejects

differences.name: wire-zero
differences.explanation: Node preserves its existing tag-zero/multiple all-outstanding interpretation. The fixed Go reference leaves handles pending until the later explicit cumulative tag; the 60 ms probe and subsequent completion are recorded separately.

differences.name: wire-future
differences.explanation: Node preserves fail-closed validation of a future broker confirmation tag. The fixed Go reference keeps the connection open and waits for a valid tag; the invalid-tag probe does not establish a broker-supported workflow.

publisherConfirmations.comparisonScope: Six controlled-peer semantic sequences and nine real broker scenarios match; exact method bytes and body hashes are checked for the matching peer sequences. Tag-zero multiple and invalid future-tag handling are explicit existing client differences. Local waiter timeout does not retract a publication. No claim of full Go channel scheduling, transport context or throughput parity.
